justification: 26 links across 23 files pointed app routes at a domain that does not serve them. One is emailed to customers, one is a JSON-LD logo, and several are canonical URLs that tell search engines where the real page lives.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: Any tracked source file contains https://plotdetect.com.au/ followed by a path, OR a JSON-LD identity url names the app subdomain. It reads the file list from git rather than the filesystem, so build output and scratch files are out of scope.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Reintroducing the granny-flat customer link: 1 failed, 3 passed. Over-correcting one JSON-LD identity url to the app subdomain: 1 failed, 3 passed. Baseline and restored both 4 passed.

pre_impl.existing_data: Measured live on 2026-08-26, both domains, every distinct path: 19 paths tested. Every one 404s on the apex. 13 return 200 on verify.plotdetect.com.au. /bushfire/ and /pre-da-history/ are prefixes that 404 bare but return 200 with a slug appended. The middleware was read to confirm it does not gate routes per host - all domains share one build and only '/' is rewritten - so the 404s are not host restrictions.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Two assumptions were wrong and both were caught by measuring. First, I concluded from the apex 404ing that the app lives on canibuildit.com.au; it does serve the app and returns 200, which made the wrong answer look confirmed. The domain doc already said to use the subdomains. Second, I assumed the rule was 'replace the host everywhere' - but layout.tsx uses the bare apex as the JSON-LD Organization url, which is correct and would have been destroyed by a blanket replace. The rule is host-plus-path, not host.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies at next deploy. Emails and reports already sent carry the dead link and cannot be corrected. Canonical URLs already crawled will re-resolve on the next crawl.

functions.name: trackedFiles
functions.input: No arguments. Runs git ls-files over frontend-nextjs, services and scripts, with every GIT_* variable stripped from the environment.
functions.output: Repo-relative paths of tracked .ts, .tsx, .py and .md files.
functions.if_none: An empty list would make the offender scan pass vacuously, so a separate assertion requires it to be non-empty before the scan is trusted.
functions.why: git is the population that ships. Scanning the filesystem would sweep in build output and untracked scratch files, and a guard was already burned once this month by policing a different population from the one that mattered. GIT_* is stripped because hooks export GIT_DIR, which overrides cwd.

values.name: APEX_WITH_PATH
values.read_at: Module load of the test file.
values.why: The lookahead is the whole point. A bare https://plotdetect.com.au is the organisation's own site and is a true statement in the JSON-LD identity block; the same host followed by a path is an app route the apex does not serve. Matching the host alone would have deleted a correct claim.

break_it.scenario: A customer is emailed their granny flat result.
break_it.what_happens: The link went to the apex, which 404s. They were told the result was ready and sent nowhere. Combined with the unawaited send fixed in #1008, this product had two independent ways to fail the same customer.
break_it.how: The link now points at verify.plotdetect.com.au, measured 200.
break_it.repro: Reintroduce the apex link -> 1 failed, 3 passed

break_it.scenario: Search engines are told where a page lives.
break_it.what_happens: Canonical URLs and the JSON-LD SearchAction named the apex. That is worse than a dead click - it actively tells a crawler the real page is at an address that 404s.
break_it.how: All canonical and structured-data app URLs now use the app subdomain.
break_it.repro: Same guard covers every tracked file, not just the route

break_it.scenario: The fix over-reaches and rewrites the organisation identity.
break_it.what_happens: layout.tsx names the bare apex as the Organization url, which is correct - that IS the company's website. A blanket host replace would have turned a true statement false.
break_it.how: The pattern requires a path after the host, and a test asserts no identity url names the app subdomain.
break_it.repro: Point one identity url at verify -> 1 failed, 3 passed

break_it.scenario: The guard sees only half of what it guards.
break_it.what_happens: The first version asserted merely that SOME bare org url survived. layout.tsx has TWO, so mutating one still passed - the guard could not detect the damage it existed to prevent.
break_it.how: Found by forcing the mutation and getting an unexpected pass. The assertion now inspects every identity line rather than looking for one survivor.
break_it.repro: Documented above - the weak version passed MUT-B, the current one fails it

post_merge.manual_verify: Two paths are broken independently of domain and are NOT fixed here: /shadow-detector is not a route at all, and /solar-potential 404s on both domains despite the route folder existing. Both are also listed in the sitemap, so the sitemap currently advertises dead pages. Separate issue, needs its own look.
